open_obligations: Note that loss of completeness without stability may still make debate useless on some questions.
Check whether cross-examination-style consistency checks were added, which Buhl et al. suggest.
Check that the safety claim holds with approximate rather than exact equilibria.
in.other_title: rho-stability assumption: needed for usefulness, not for safety
in.rationale: Buhl et al. ask for protocols that do not require stability, since it may not hold for relevant queries. Brown-Cohen et al. state rho-stability is required only for usefulness (completeness), not for safety: without it an honest estimator can still beat any incorrect argument by a dishonest prover; it does not address the gerrymandering concern across subclaims.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether the stability assumption of prover-estimator debate is needed for safety, for recursive debate

text: The authors ask for protocols that do not require stability, since it might not hold for relevant queries, for example by targeting honesty instead of correctness or by transforming an unstable computation into a stable one. They also note that cross-examination punishes debaters for inconsistency across claims at the same recursive level while prover-estimator debate does not, and suggest combining these protocols or finding other solutions.
title: Open: relax the stability assumption and avoid gerrymandering across subclaims
